episodes.205553: Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon, producing isolated wind damage and small hail.
episodes.205557: A severe thunderstorm brought large hail to northeast Valley county.
episodes.205669: A cluster of severe thunderstorms developed near the Wyoming and Nebraska border during the late afternoon hours on Sepgtember 10th. Hail up to the size of golf balls were reported with these storms.
episodes.206519: Monsoon thunderstorms became strong enough to produce some severe downburst winds in a couple locations.
episodes.207000: Well above normal temperatures and an extended period of dry conditions (prompting a D2 drought for Crittenden County), enabled a dust devil to form on the 11th, which attracted significant public attention as it developed next to a Crittenden County Middle School classroom. Wind shear was modest, around 20kts, leaving microscale factors as the primary drivers of dust devil formation.
episodes.207247: The combination of an upper-level trough over the west coast and the subtropical high situated over Texas resulted in a southwesterly steering flow. With PWATs ranging between 1.0-1.2 and MLCAPE values approaching 1000 J/kg, afternoon thunderstorms developed across the eastern third of AZ with some of the activity affecting southern Gila County, including the San Carlos area. With DCAPE in excess of 1000 J/kg, conditions were conducive for these thunderstorms to produce strong to severe wind gusts.
episodes.207383: Slow-moving, late afternoon into early evening thunderstorms associated with the sea breeze and a stationary frontal boundary across the central peninsula produce heavy rainfall that leads to street flooding near Fort Myers in Lee County.
episodes.207505: A thunderstorm developed over the Wind River Mountain and moved toward Lander, producing strong wind gusts. The highest wind gust reported was 78 mph in the higher elevations to the southwest of Lander. The Lander airport had a maximum wind gust of 69 mph.
episodes.207506: There were two rounds of severe thunderstorm winds on this day. The first occurred early in the morning as a high based shower collapsed near the Natrona County airport and produced a 67 mph wind gust. The second round occurred near Lander when thunderstorms produced a 66 mph wind gust at the Lander airport.
episodes.207517: A boundary stretching east from a surface low pressure system in northwest North Dakota combined with the northern tip of a low level jet to produce thunderstorms over north central North Dakota. Some of these storms became severe producing large hail. The largest hail was two inches in diameter, and fell near Granville in McHenry County.
episodes.207548: An outflow boundary from strong thunderstorms over the southern mainland of Florida moved southward, producing gale-force wind gusts in the coastal waters near Key Largo.
episodes.207727: The period between the 11th and 13th of September had a relatively unique meteorological setup for western Colorado and eastern Utah. A potent closed low was located over Southern California, and a ridge of high pressure was located to our southeast, directing a rich plume of monsoonal moisture northward through the Four Corners. Mixing ratios in this plume of moisture were more than high enough to not only help form strong to severe thunderstorms, but also to produce flash flooding and debris flows. Additionally, there was ample instability, with morning clearing helping 600-1000 J/kg of CAPE develop each afternoon. The region also fell under the right exit region of a potent upper level jet streak, which added additional lift and 40-50 kts of shear. Additionally, terrain effects added additional lift and shear. All together, this was a potent setup with the potential to produce severe thunderstorms. And indeed, the storms that developed produced not only large hail and strong, damaging winds, but also two tornadoes in Southeast Utah, and flash flooding across the area. Particularly, fresh burn scars, including the Lee and Elk RBX scars, saw substantial flash flooding and debris flows as storms trained over the area and produced very heavy rain. Finally, after 3 days of widespread severe weather, the cold front pushed through the region, and a cooler, drier, and above all, calmer airmass moved in, bringing an end to the event.

episodes.207769: Slow moving thunderstorms produced flash flooding and hail across portions of the Devils Lake basin.
episodes.207781: A surface boundary over Central Florida with influence from a mid level shortwave trough led to diurnal showers and thunderstorms developing over Southeast Florida on the 11th and 12th of September.
episodes.207844: A severe thunderstorm tracked across northern Weld County during the afternoon of the 11th producing hail up to 1.5 inch in diameter.
episodes.207963: A severe thunderstorm caused wind damage in West Carroll Parish.
episodes.208340: A few thunderstorms become strong to severe over the evening and produced marginal severe weather across Pennington and Box Elder counties.
